subject: Recap: Finlytics discovery — inference cost, batching & PoC next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Luke Harper <luke.harper@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Nov 2025 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Finlytics discovery — inference cost, batching & PoC next steps

Hi Luke / Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Wanted to capture the key points and suggested next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve kept this focused on unit-economics and technical constraints that will shape the PoC.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- High inference spend driven by many small requests (median batch size: ~1) and long contexts (up to 8k tokens for analysis flows).
- Current infra uses GCP T4s behind an internal Triton stack; you’ve observed inconsistent KV caching and no prefix caching across sessions.
- Hesitancy to quantize because of model-quality concerns for rare-fact extraction use cases.
- Need predictable per-invocation cost for budgeting and SRE-friendly SLAs (monthly forecasted spend variance >30% currently).

Current stack (as discussed):
- Model hosting: in-house Triton on GCP (T4 fleet), some offline HF endpoints for experimentation.
- Frontend: request fan-out from microservices, average payload ~350 tokens, heavy tail to 3.5k tokens.
- Monitoring: basic Prometheus metrics; no token-level cost tracking today.

Success criteria for an acceptable PoC / pilot:
1) Achieve at least 30% reduction in per-token cost for typical production traffic (workload you shared) while maintaining answer quality (<=3% regression on your extraction F1).
2) End-to-end P95 latency at or below 750ms for 95% of requests in the key path.
3) Demonstrate stable batching and prefix/KV caching that materially reduces GPU cycles for repeat prompts.
4) Deliver a reproducible benchmark report (token-level cost, latency distributions, quality regression delta).

Recommended next steps (proposed timeline):
- Redwood: prepare PoC plan & benchmark harness (attached: redwood-poc-plan.pdf + benchmark instructions). Aditya will run a 48–72 hour benchmark against a representative sample you provide.
- Finlytics: share a sanitized sample traffic dump and a short eval set (10–20 golden examples) for quality checks. You mentioned GCS is preferred — please confirm link and permissions.
- Tech sync: schedule an infra/ops session (30–45m) with your SREs to walk Triton deployment and access. Marcus to lead.
- Decision point: If we hit the cost/latency bars, we scope a 6-week pilot on Dedicated capacity.

Questions for you:
1) Are you comfortable with a targeted quality regression of up to 3% on extractive metrics if we can reach the cost goals?
2) Can you share a GCS path with ~48–72 hours of representative traffic (or a synthetic generator we can run)?

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf; mutual-action-plan.xlsx; redwood-benchmark-instructions.md

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the infra sync once you confirm permissions.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0186

From: Luke Harper <luke.harper@finlytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Nov 2025 09:54:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Finlytics discovery — inference cost, batching & PoC next steps

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That matches our notes. A few clarifications: 
- We currently run on GCP T4s (not A100s) with Triton. Our traffic is spiky; median batch size ~1 confirmed.
- We’re willing to tolerate up to ~3% drop on the extraction F1 for common queries, but for our regulatory reports (1% of traffic) we need near-zero regression. We can mark those examples in the eval set.
- I uploaded a sanitized 72-hour sample to GCS here: https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/finlytics-test-data/sample-traffic/ (read access granted to redwood-poc@redwood.com).

I attached our SOC2 extract and a high-level network diagram (soc2-answers.pdf).

Next steps from our side:
- Confirm infra sync window — Wed 11/12 (US/PST) looks good for our SREs.
- We’d prefer the PoC to start the week of 11/11 and run 10 business days.

Luke
Senior Engineering Manager | Finlytics
luke.harper@finlytics.com | +1 (415) 555-2299

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Luke Harper <luke.harper@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Finlytics discovery — inference cost, batching & PoC next steps

Perfect — thanks Luke, that GCS link and SOC2 doc are exactly what we need.

We’ll proceed as follows: 
- Aditya will drop the benchmark harness into your GCS bucket and run the 48–72 hour run starting Tuesday 11/11 at 09:00 PST. Expect an initial baseline (no quantization, default Triton config) then a second run with batching + prefix caching enabled.
- Marcus will join the infra sync on Wed 11/12 at 10:00 PST to validate Triton access and any network egress rules. Marcus will share the invite via calendar (link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=vanessa_finlytics_poc_start_20251111).
- If the baseline shows >25% unit-cost uplift vs. current (i.e., things are worse), we’ll stop and regroup. If we get >=30% cost reduction in the optimized run and quality is within your constraints, we’ll propose Dedicated capacity sizing and an estimated commit.

I’m attaching the benchmark instructions we’ll run (redwood-benchmark-instructions.md) and the mutual action plan.

If that timeline works on your end I’ll send the infra invite and a short pre-run checklist for your SREs.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0186
